Games and the relay now have to be up to date to play together, so a version missing a fix can't get in. Relay 1.6.0 goes with it.

**Up to date to play online**
- Every game (desktop, phone and the web page) now says its version when it connects, and the relay turns away versions older than it allows. The oldest let in is 1.25.4 unless the relay's keeper sets otherwise in the console (VERSIONS); raising it lets go of anyone connected with an older game.
- A game that's too old says so ("update it to play online"), and the desktop app looks for the update straight away (and installs it, if *Install automatically* is on). It doesn't wander off to another relay, and tries again after half an hour.
- Games from before 1.25.4 can't say they're too old: they simply can't connect to the village's relay until they're updated.
- The relay also says its own version. A game connected to a relay older than 1.6.0 (a community's own, say) tells its player that the relay is out of date.

**The relay (1.6.0)**
- A connection the relay lets go (too slow, kicked, banned) now ends at once, and what was waiting for it is let go with it. Tested against a local relay: 23 readers that never read, sent 100 KB messages as fast as allowed, peaked at 54 MB and were back to 7 MB within seconds. Before 1.5.0 the same flood would have run it out of memory.
- The updater starts the relay and host again only when an image has really changed, and its daily update now runs at 07:30 UTC.
